One reviewer measured each of the 21 pockets as 7.5 inches high and 7 inches wide, with each pocket subdivided by overlaid mesh into inner and outer compartments. [1]

The reviews don't confirm this.

Reviewers describe the clear part of the container as clear hard plastic, not glass. [1][2]

Verdict: Reviews disagree

Another reviewer says the bottom of the StrongArm strut turns so it can be adjusted for either side, and that the part fits both left and right sides. [2]

Verdict: Yes
A reviewer with a 2014 Wrangler Unlimited Sport says the hitch fit, though Amazon showed a 'will not fit your vehicle' notice; the maker's website listed fit for 2007-2014 models. [1]
Another reviewer with a 2014 Wrangler Sport Unlimited says the hitch fit perfectly. [2]

Reviewers disagree on sizing: some say the glasses run small or fit tightly on small heads and cause headaches, while others say they fit large heads or are too large for small faces. [1][2]
One reviewer with a small face and petite frame says they fit well and do not leak wind or slip. [3]
One reviewer with a much smaller head than the reviewer's friend says the glasses looked fine on the friend and caused no watering-eye complaints. [4]
One reviewer says a woman with a small face found them too large, while her husband liked them. [2]
One reviewer with a medium-sized head says they fit well, and warns that people with large heads may not get a comfortable fit. [5]
A reviewer with a 5'9" average build says they fit well and that fit depends on head size. [6]

Verdict: Yes
Some reviewers say the iron was supposed to come with a special comb according to other reviews, but one reviewer's unit came with neither the floating plates nor the comb. [1]
Reviewers who received the iron describe a comb that comes with it; one reviewer calls the comb amazing and says it is a staple to liking the flat iron. [2][3]
One reviewer says the included comb is not high quality material and they are concerned about how long it will hold up. [3]
One reviewer says the comb grips the hair tightly, which the flat iron alone does not do, making the comb key to the results. [4]
Reviewers say the iron is a Jose Eber model sold through kiosks and Amazon, and that the Amazon-bought units arrived brand new. [3][5]

Verdict: Yes
One reviewer says the sleeve fit their 14-inch Lenovo U430 Touch well, and it still fits when the computer is in a hard shell case. [1][2]
Another reviewer says it fits a 13-inch MacBook perfectly, and it is described as protective for travel and daily use. [3]
Several reviewers say the fit is perfect, including for a hard-to-find size. [4][5][6][7]

Verdict: No
The headphones have no built-in volume control on the headset itself; reviewers say volume must be adjusted on the connected device. [1][2][3]
A reviewer says a Koss V20 Volume Control Extender can be bought separately under $10 to adjust volume, but another reviewer found it did not noticeably increase the volume, so it is not a reliable fix. [1]
A reviewer says a separate volume controller costing about $5 can be used if the sound is too loud when connected to a TV, which suggests an external option rather than a built-in control. [4]
Some reviewers wish the headphones had an inline or on-cable volume control, and one says they would have rated them higher with one. [5][6]

Verdict: Yes
Several reviewers say they leave the product in overnight and rinse it out in the morning, and report softer, shinier hair afterward. [1][2][3]
One reviewer applies it after washing, covers hair with a shower cap or bandana, sleeps with it on, and rinses it out in the morning; they say their very dry hair felt like silk afterward. [2][4]
One reviewer with curly hair that was blow-dried straight leaves the product on overnight, then washes and styles the hair the next day and reports curls back to normal and non-frizzy. [5]
Reviewers describe overnight use mostly on hair that was washed first or is wet; the excerpts do not clearly describe application to fully dry hair. [2][6][3]
One reviewer with very dry hair left the mask on for 10 to 30 minutes and reported no improvement, and said a family member had the same result; these excerpts do not describe overnight use. [7]

Verdict: Yes
Multiple reviewers say the case has good padding or cushioning that protects the laptop. [1][2][3][4]
One reviewer says the padding is just right to protect the laptop from damage. [1]
One reviewer describes the cushioning as nice and says it compares favorably to higher priced Apple store cases. [2]
One reviewer says the padding is not too thick, but enough to protect the laptop while it is out and in a backpack. [3]
One reviewer says the case gives extra padding and protected the laptop from stray pens and other items, though it is not waterproof. [5]
One reviewer says the case provides some cushion to protect the laptop. [6]
One reviewer says the case has cushioning on the inside for protection. [7]

The excerpts describe the Moroccanoil Intense Hydrating Mask, not the Restorative Hair Mask, so no direct comparison between the two is made. [1]
Reviewers describe the Intense Hydrating Mask as heavy and greasy for fine or thin hair, and one reviewer recommends the lighter Moroccanoil Conditioner instead. [2]
Reviewers describe the Intense Hydrating Mask as hydrating and softening, with one reviewer saying it works well on coarse thick hair and others saying it left oily residue or weighed hair down. [3][4][5]

Verdict: Yes
One reviewer says the hooks fold in flat, so the rack can be slid between a washer and the wall or hidden behind a hamper in a closet when not in use. [1]
Not covered by the reviews: Whether the rack folds completely flat or collapses for storage (reviewer only says the hooks fold in flat); Whether the main frame folds or is only the hooks that fold

Verdict: Yes
Multiple reviewers report that the memory installed in a Dell Inspiron 6000 and worked well, with one saying it was immediately recognized by the BIOS. [1][2]
Reviewers say the memory noticeably sped up their Dell Inspiron 6000, including one who upgraded it from 0.5 GB to 2 GB and ran Windows 7. [3][4][5]
One reviewer with a Dell Inspiron 6400 reported needing to reset the memory before it was recognized, which is a different model from the 6000. [6]
One reviewer noted that additional memory beyond this upgrade would not be used in the Inspiron 6000. [7]

Verdict: Can't confirm
One reviewer opened the package and found the packaging torn where it would normally be removed, as if the straightener had already been opened and used. [1]
Another reviewer received the iron without a clear retail box; it arrived with a poorly glued sticker, and they doubted it was genuine after examining it. [2]
One reviewer said the iron arrived with scratches and was smaller than the seller described, and they doubted it was original or authentic. [3]
One reviewer said the item was delivered with a different product than ordered, a curling iron instead of a straightening iron. [4]
Not covered by the reviews: Whether the product comes in its original box: reviewers mention packaging that was torn, opened, or a product that was used or without a clear box, but none confirm an intact original retail box

Reviewers report that the sleeve fits laptops of various sizes well, including 11.5 to 15.6 inch laptops, and some note a snug or perfect fit. [1][2][3][4]
One reviewer says a Surface 2 fits the sleeve very well in size. [5]
One reviewer reports that a Yoga 2 Pro (13 x 8 5/8 x 9/16 inches) fits the case like a glove and that the case could be a bit larger in depth before the zipper has issues. [6]
A reviewer says a 15 inch sleeve was too large for a 14 7/8 x 10 inch Dell Inspiron 15Z, and the 14 inch sleeve fit snugly but was hard to zip. [7][8]
Another reviewer found a 15 inch sleeve about one inch too wide for a MacBook Pro 15 inch and said it slides around a little. [9]
A reviewer found a 13.3 inch-rated case a little roomy for a 13 inch MacBook Pro. [10]

Verdict: No
One reviewer bought an extra dock-and-play kit for work and home, which suggests the dock/home kit is bought separately from the radio. [1]
Another reviewer says they needed a separate radio to go with the dock, which suggests the dock is not included with the radio. [2]
One reviewer had to buy a 50-foot antenna cable for the house because they had no clear view to the south, which suggests a longer antenna cable is an extra purchase. [1]
Reviewers describe the home kit as a separate accessory. One reviewer liked it and planned to use it with their stereo; another found the FM transmitter does not work when used with the Home Kit. [3][4]
One reviewer moved the antenna around until the signal locked in, and another replaced the antenna without fixing a fault, so the antenna appears to be a separate, replaceable part. [5][6]

Not covered by the reviews: Whether the radio package includes the antenna; Whether the powerdock (home kit) is included with the radio or sold separately

Verdict: No
One reviewer noticed that the oil is not cold pressed, but said it still works pretty well as a moisturizer. [1]

Verdict: Yes
Multiple reviewers with color-treated hair say the product works well on it, describing softer, moisturized hair after use. [1][2][3]
One reviewer uses it as a deep conditioner on dry, relaxed, color-treated hair mixed with olive oil, left on for an hour without heat, and says it is fabulous. [4]
One reviewer with coarse, color-treated hair uses it twice a week and says it saves the day. [5]
One reviewer applies it before swimming to protect color-treated hair from pool chemicals. [6]
One reviewer with very dry hair from coloring says the mask left hair soft and well-conditioned without residue after use as a weekly treatment. [7]
One reviewer with fine, color-treated hair says the light version of the Moroccan Oil treatment is made for fine or color-treated hair, and they use that version. [8]

Verdict: Yes
One reviewer hung the organizer on a rod in the closet for hangers and said it was workable if you can reach both sides, so it could be hung back to back in the same spot. [1]
One reviewer could not hang it on the door after moving and found a place to hang it in the closet instead. [2]
Several reviewers hung it on the back or inside of a closet door, or screwed or attached it to a wall, rather than on a rod. [3][4][5]
Some reviewers say the hooks do not fit over thicker doors, and one reviewer suggests screwing it to a door or wall instead. [6][7]
Not covered by the reviews: No excerpt confirms hanging the organizer from a closet rod with its hooks, which is the method the shopper asked about; Reviewers describe the closet door or the wall, not a closet rod

One reviewer states the tray measures 12in x 5in. [1]
Several reviewers describe the tray as small, smaller than they expected from the online photos, and not suited to a full-size dresser or as a show piece. [2][3][4][5][6]
Reviewers say the tray fits about 6 to 7 perfumes. [7][1][6]
One reviewer suggests it is best for a child's dresser, a restroom, or as a small accent piece rather than a vanity. [7][4]

Multiple reviewers who own a 2005 Jeep Grand Cherokee report these lift supports fit that model and work well after installation. [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][8]
A reviewer who owns a 2005 Jeep Grand Cherokee Laredo 4x4 with a 4.7L engine described this product as a perfect fit for that exact trim. [1]
One reviewer with a 2008 Grand Cherokee reported that a listing saying it would not work on that model fit and worked, and guessed it would also fit 2009 and 2010 models; this is a reviewer's guess, not confirmed. [9]
A reviewer noted the product is listed for 05-10 Grand Cherokee WK models, and another reviewer said it fit a 2006 Grand Cherokee, indicating fit across several model years. [10][11]
Some reviewers report that the left and right supports are side-specific, and one reviewer said one side-specific unit only fits the left side. [12][13]
Several reviewers say the installation takes about 10 to 20 minutes per pair and needs a T40 Torx bit and a second person to hold up the liftgate. [14][4][15][16]
One reviewer reported that the supports were sold separately and that they had to buy two. [17]
One reviewer said the product was not returnable or received the wrong part and was charged a restocking fee, though this was about a different order. [18]
The reviews don't confirm this.

Reviewers say the copper finish patinas/tarnishes quickly, in some cases within about a year, and one reviewer's pair ended up with one mill almost completely tarnished while the other stayed nearly perfect. [1][2]
One reviewer says a good cleaning with copper cleaner did not completely fix the tarnish. [1]
Reviewers recommend cleaning with Brasso or another cleaner at least once every six months if you want to keep the shine. [3]
One reviewer says that to keep the bright copper look you must clean the mills very diligently, while others say they don't worry about the patina and let it develop. [2][3]
One reviewer says the copper coating eventually tarnishes in spots as the lacquer wears away, and that the coating should have been left off. [4]

Verdict: Yes
Multiple reviewers say the product helps dry, frizzy hair in winter, with one reporting it calms dry frizzy hairs and visible effects lasting two or three days. [1][2][3]
A reviewer reports that the product reduces frizz in rain and humidity and gives immediate shine. [4]
A reviewer with dry, chemically treated hair says it immediately helped with dryness and flyaways. [5]
One reviewer says the softness lasts only until the hair gets wet, and they think the product coats the hair rather than moisturizing it. [6]
A reviewer says a tiny amount applied to the driest parts of hair lasts a long time and works well. [7]
The reviews don't confirm this.

Verdict: Yes
Reviewers say the pads remove makeup well, including eye makeup; one reviewer says the soft side removes eye makeup and mascara. [1][2][3]
Reviewers say the soft side is gentle enough for eye makeup while the textured side exfoliates the rest of the face. [4][5]
One reviewer says the pads removed all makeup residue, and another says they remove any eye makeup they put on, even after cutting a pad in half. [3][6]
Reviewers say the pads are a convenient travel option for removing makeup, since a couple in a zip bag can replace a large jar. [7]

Verdict: Can't confirm
One reviewer applied the vinyl to plastic buckets, a plastic drinking cup, a water bottle and a toilet lid, and reported that it peeled off, so reviewers did not find it stays permanently attached on these surfaces. [1][2]
Another reviewer reported the vinyl was perfect for wrapping a lap top and working with a jar, and that it removes without residue or with minimal residue, but these reviews do not describe painted surfaces. [3][4]
Removal is reported as clean with no residue in some reviews, and one reviewer said the vinyl peels off easily without residue. [3][4]
Not covered by the reviews: Whether the vinyl can be used on painted surfaces (reviews only mention plastic buckets, a plastic cup, a water bottle and a toilet lid); Whether the vinyl can be removed after a couple of years without staining (reviews only describe removal after days or a few months, with one saying it peels off easily without residue)

Verdict: Reviews disagree
One reviewer said the cover was water tight in the rain and only a very small amount of water got in while going through a high pressure car wash. [1]
One reviewer drove through a high pressure car wash right after installing the cover and found only minor drips inside after the dry cycle. [2]
One reviewer reported some water getting by in a drive-thru car wash, but not much. [3]
One reviewer found water by the tailgate and front of the bed after a car wash, which they attributed partly to the car wash spraying sideways; they planned to retest with a hose. [4]
One reviewer reported some water leakage between the cover gasket and the tailgate on trucks with a built-in tailgate step, which they were working to fix. [5]
Reviewers' experiences are mixed: most report the cover is largely watertight, while some report water getting in during car washes or in rain. [1][4][3]

Verdict: Yes
One reviewer says the iron constantly turns itself off while in use after it stopped working, which they attribute possibly to stuck buttons. [1]
A reviewer says that after months of use the iron started shutting off and coming back on, then changing temperatures, which they describe as a malfunction. [2]
A reviewer says the iron turns off unexpectedly while they are working with their hair, and they did not consider this a safety feature. [3]
Not covered by the reviews: Whether the product has a dedicated safety auto shut-off feature stated by the manufacturer; reviewers only describe the iron turning off unexpectedly, which reads as a malfunction rather than a documented safety feature

Verdict: Reviews disagree
Several reviewers say the mitt becomes hard to handle or heavy when full of soapy water, especially for those with smaller hands. [1][2][3][4]
One reviewer says it can get a little heavy when wet, which can be tiring when washing a larger car or multiple cars. [2]
One reviewer describes it as clunky and heavy, saying it is not worth it compared with microfiber towels. [3]
Other reviewers say it holds a lot of water and soap but is not too heavy, and one says it is super light and does not fatigue the arm even though it holds lots of soap and water. [4][5][6]

One reviewer says these are the same glasses sold at a Harley Davidson dealership for $20 a pair and that they are the same great glasses at a third of the cost. [1]
Another reviewer says they bought the tinted sunglasses at a local dealership for $20 and found these on Amazon, which they describe as the same exact brand, at $16 for three. [2]
A reviewer says these are the same price they paid for one pair at their local motorcycle dealer and that the quality is the same. [3]
Reviewers say these glasses are sold at motorcycle shops for about $20 each and seem to be good quality. [4]
Reviewers say the glasses are a good value and are durable, fit well for some heads, and work as well as name-brand glasses costing $100 or more. [5]
Some reviewers say the glasses fit poorly and let wind in, depending on head size, and one reviewer says the lenses are too small for speeds above 20 mph. [6][7][5]
Reviewers say the clear, smoke and yellow lenses cover different riding conditions and that the three-pair set is a good package. [8][9][10]
Not covered by the reviews: The model number stamped on the clear lens frame is not mentioned in any excerpt.

Reviewers describe the wiring harness as plug-and-play, connecting to the factory tail light plug without splicing or cutting. [1][2][3][4]
Reviewers report the wiring harness worked and the lights and everything on the Jeep functioned after installation. [5][6]
Reviewers say the harness is easy to install and looks factory-like. [7][6][8]
Not covered by the reviews: Whether the harness works without a ground cable wire specifically; reviewers describe plug-and-play connection and working lights but do not mention a separate ground cable

Verdict: Can't confirm
One reviewer says the coil pack fits great. [1]
A reviewer says that after installing the coil pack, the check engine light was removed. [2]
A reviewer says the coil pack cost half the price of a Dodge dealership. [2]
A reviewer says the coil fixed a #3 coil pack code. [1]

Several reviewers say the product must be bought in pairs: one reviewer notes that the lift supports are sold separately and that you have to buy two. [1][2]
Reviewers say the supports are sold individually and that both sides are needed for a full repair: one reviewer ordered two and says one replacement was enough for the gate to hold up, while another says the item fits only the left side and a second part is needed for the right side. [3][2]
Many reviewers replaced both supports at once, and the manual reportedly says to replace in pairs. [4][5]
One reviewer replaced only one strut and found the gate still held up while keeping an easy-to-open gate, suggesting a single support can be enough in some cases. [6][2]

Verdict: Yes
Reviewers say the receiver attaches to the camera's hot shoe and the remote's receiver can be mounted there, but a reviewer who wanted to use the camera's flash attachment could not use the shoe mount and instead attached the receiver to the tripod with velcro. [1]
A reviewer who uses the remote's receiver with an off-camera flash says they chose a radio transmitter/receiver over TTL cords to fire their flash off camera, which suggests radio triggering for flash is a use reviewers have made of this type of system. [2]
The receiver has a hot shoe clip that attaches it on top of the camera, and the package includes a stick-on plastic hot shoe for use on a tripod. [3]
This is a close case: the excerpts do not show whether a separate radio flash trigger can share the hot shoe with this remote's receiver, so the yes answer is only partly supported. [1][3]
Not covered by the reviews: Whether a separate radio flash trigger can be mounted in the hot shoe while this remote's receiver is attached, or whether the receiver occupies the shoe; Whether the radio flash trigger fires the flash correctly while the remote's receiver is connected

Verdict: Yes
Multiple reviewers say this vinyl works with the Silhouette Cameo and report no issues using it with that machine. [1][2][3]
Reviewers have used the vinyl on the Cameo for projects such as monograms on plastic and ceramic items, plant markers, tumblers, and ornaments. [4][5][6]

Reviewers describe the LED lamp in this kit as working well and reliably; one reviewer says it still works perfectly about six months after purchase. [1][2]
One reviewer's cord was not long enough to reach the outlet and needed an extension cord, which indicates the lamp is plugged into a wall outlet. [3]
One reviewer found the LED light not quite big enough to fit a whole hand, so thumbs had to be done separately. [2]
One reviewer's lamp stopped working, and the vendor replaced the kit. [4]

Verdict: Yes
No reviewer mentions the DMC-FZ70 specifically; the closest reported models are the FZ100, FZ150 and FZ200, and reviewers say the remote worked on those. [1][2][3]
Reviewers report the remote works on the Panasonic DMC-FZ150 once the cable ends are seated correctly and the small switches in both battery chambers are set to the same position. [1]

Verdict: Can't confirm
The reviews don't confirm this.

Verdict: Yes

One reviewer says it is handmade by real people in Greece. [4]

Verdict: Yes
Several reviewers say dark spots or acne scarring faded or diminished after using the product, with one reviewer reporting fading after about two weeks. [1][2][3]
A reviewer with dark spots and fine lines reported that their dark spots and blotches improved after using the discs for about a month, with the reviewer also using a separate night cream. [4][5]

Verdict: Can't confirm
One reviewer who had used Josie Maran argan oil before says the NOW argan oil is a little heavier and does not dissipate as fast when applied, so it does not give the same luxurious feel; they said it is not a big deal but matters to them, and they have no other complaints about it. [1]

Verdict: Yes
One reviewer says the memory fitted perfectly in their Dell Inspiron 6400 and made the computer faster. [1]
A reviewer installed the modules in their INSPIRON 6400, ran the diagnostic, and reports they are working perfectly. [2]

Reviewers say the mirror tray is small: 12in x 5in, smaller than many expected from the online photos. [1][2][3]
One reviewer says it is best on a child's dresser or vanity or as a small accent piece, and would not look good on a full-size dresser. [4]
Reviewers describe the tray as very pretty, with gorgeous jewels and detailed butterfly and orchid designs. [5][6]

Reviewers report the UniFi AP gives strong range; one user with a 2300 sq ft two-story house said it fixed upstairs connectivity after connecting it to an existing router and disabling that router's WiFi. [1]
One reviewer connected the UniFi AP to an existing Uverse set-top box via an Ethernet cable and a PoE adapter, reporting signal improved from two bars to five. [2]

One reviewer recommended pairing the UniFi AP with a separate Gigabit router, such as the TL-R600VPN, for a combined cost of about $130. [6]
One reviewer paired an EdgeRouter Lite with the UniFi AP and needed to adjust IP ranges to use the WAN+2LAN wizard. [7]
Reviewers describe setup as easy on some systems but some report difficulty; one reviewer's configuration software would not run on a Win7 64-bit computer, which appears to be a known issue. [5][2][8]
Reviewers say the AP needs a PoE adapter, and that Ethernet cables must be supplied by the buyer since none are included. [3][2]
Not covered by the reviews: No excerpt says whether the Motorola SB6121 modem works with the UniFi AP; the excerpts only describe connecting the AP to an existing router or a PoE adapter.; Excerpts do not state what type of router to recommend for home use or confirm the SB6121 as a router.; Whether a separate router is needed alongside a modem and UniFi AP is only partly covered: reviewers used existing routers, a Uverse box, or a Gigabit router with the AP, but none addresses the SB6121 specifically.

Verdict: Yes
Reviewers describe the product as a wireless access point, not a router; one reviewer says it must be plugged into an existing working network and will not work plugged directly into a DSL or cable modem. [1][2]
One reviewer used it with a wired router for cable internet and another plugged it into a wired gateway router and got it running quickly, with full coverage in their home. [3][4]
Reviewers say it needs a wired Ethernet connection to the router or switch and does not bridge a wireless connection from a wireless router. [5]
Reviewers say the device is powered over Ethernet, so a single cable run can supply power and network, and that it does not include Ethernet cables. [5][4]
